source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: China's DUV machine development is a real phase transition but the market overreacted; it will take decades to close the gap with EUV
summary_extended: Baker argues that China's development of a DUV lithography machine represents a meaningful technological milestone — a 'phase transition' in capability — but that the market dramatically overreacted by selling off semiconductor capital equipment stocks. He uses the analogy of a propeller plane (DUV) versus a jet turbine (EUV) to illustrate that China remains approximately 25 years behind the leading edge, and that the learning-by-doing process required to close that gap cannot be artificially accelerated. Baker contends that even if China's DUV progress eventually threatens ASML's order book, that impact is likely 5 or more years away, and the market will have cycled through multiple rounds of worry and forgetting before it materializes. The investment implication is that the selloff in semi-cap equipment names — particularly ASML — was an overreaction and potentially a buying opportunity, though Baker acknowledges the development should not be entirely dismissed.
detail: China developing a DUV machine is significant — a phase transition from 'liquid to solid' — but DUV is like a propeller plane vs. EUV's jet turbine. China is ~25 years behind. Learning-by-doing cannot be accelerated; you have to go through the cycles. The market massively overreacted in semi-cap equipment stocks. If it ever hits ASML's orders, it may be 5 years away, and the market will have forgotten and re-worried multiple times by then.
confidence_evidence: Baker says 'probably an overreaction' but also 'we shouldn't dismiss it either'; balanced view
quote_fragment: DUV machine is like a propeller plane, EUV is like a jet turbine... 25 years behind

ticker_audit.reasoning: ASML is the direct subject of this thesis — Baker explicitly discusses the potential (but distant) threat to ASML's order book from China's DUV development and argues the selloff in ASML was an overreaction.

KLAC is a leading semi-cap equipment company that would have been caught in the same selloff Baker describes as an overreaction; as a major process control equipment supplier, it is a direct beneficiary of the thesis that the selloff was overdone.

LRCX is a major semi-cap equipment company similarly affected by fears of Chinese lithography self-sufficiency; Baker's thesis that the market overreacted to China's DUV news implies the selloff in names like LRCX was also excessive.

AMAT is the largest US-listed semi-cap equipment company and would be directly implicated in any broad selloff of the sector driven by China DUV fears; Baker's overreaction thesis applies to this group.
